title: Composable region-tier routing and graceful model-variant fallback refactor
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary: Refactor the policy engine to support composable routing blocks (region, tier, capability, cost) and deterministic fallback selection among model variants. The goal is to replace ad-hoc routing rules with a typed, composable DSL -> IR -> runtime pipeline that validates config at commit time, provides safe staged migration, and guarantees deterministic fallbacks for availability and cost-based degradations.

Goals:
- Introduce a composable rule AST that separates region affinity, tier constraints, and fallback policies into orthogonal blocks (RegionBlock, TierBlock, FallbackChain).
- Strong schema validation with helpful errors: unknown fields, deprecated keys, and model-variant compatibility checks.
- Deterministic fallback algorithm: explicit match -> region-weighted selection -> cost-preferring variant -> quantized-compat fallback -> CPU fallback.
- Migration tooling: automatic converter from legacy routing DSL, with a validation pass and opt-in compatibility shim.
- Observability hooks: per-request routing trace, fallback reason tags, and route-satisfaction metrics for rollout gating.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Typed AST vs. pure JSON schema: choose typed AST (statically validated) to enable compile-time transforms (e.g., expand shorthand, inject region defaults). This increases upfront implementation time but simplifies downstream runtime code and error messages.
- Strict validation by default with opt-in permissive mode: strict mode prevents silent semantics changes for customers; permissive mode exists for staged migration.
- Deterministic fallback order is opinionated (region affinity before cost) because customers expect locality SLAs; provide config hooks to reverse preference per-route if needed.
- We will not attempt global optimization (NP-hard) in this iteration — leave cost-aware global routing for a follow-up.

Acceptance criteria:
- New parser emits typed IR for all existing routing configs without changing request behavior when run under compatibility shim.
- Linter and schema validator run in CI and in-console policy editor; unknown fields cause errors in strict mode.
- End-to-end integration test coverage for: primary route hit, single-variant failure -> fallback variant selected, region-unavailable -> regional fallback behavior, tier overload -> degrade to lower-tier variant.
- Observability: dashboard tile showing fallback-rate, avg latency delta post-fallback, and per-region route-satisfaction.
- Rollout plan implemented in console with canary gating and automatic rollback on fallback-rate > 1%.

Migration plan:
1) Implement parser and IR, enable permissive compatibility mode for existing configs.
2) Provide automatic conversion tool (cli/tooling) that suggests rewritten rules and a diff-able preview.
3) Run staged migration on internal tenants, then beta customers who opt in.
4) After 6 weeks of metrics stability, flip default to strict validation and remove compatibility shim in 3 months.

Telemetry & Metrics:
- metric.routing.fallback_rate{route,account,region} (count/total)
- metric.routing.fallback_latency_delta_ms (histogram)
- metric.routing.policy_validation_failures{error_type}
- metric.routing.topology_mismatch_count (per region)

Testing strategy:
- Property-based tests for parser -> IR roundtrip with random valid and intentionally malformed inputs.
- Fuzzer harness for routing policy permutations (leverage existing routing-spec-emulator).
- Integration tests against runtime with model-variant simulation (introduce synthetic model failures and region blackholes).
- End-to-end performance tests ensuring <5% median latency increase at 95th percentile p99 under typical traffic when using new engine.

Rollout plan & SLO gates:
- Canary: internal only (1% traffic) for 48h, observe fallback_rate < 0.5% and p99 latency delta < 3%.
- Beta: 5 customers, 10% traffic for 1 week, fallback_rate < 1%, errors < 0.1%.
- Gradual ramp to 100% over 2 weeks with nightly health checks and automatic rollback on gate breach.

Implementation notes / file references:
- Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RI/Composable+Routing+AST+Design
- Conversion tool prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tools/pull/282 (WIP)
- Runtime integration PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1347 (draft)
acceptance_criteria:
1) Parser + typed IR produced for all legacy configs under compatibility mode.
2) CI linter prevents unknown keys in strict mode.
3) Integration tests demonstrate deterministic fallback behavior across region and tier failures.
4) Dashboard with fallback-rate and latency-delta visible and used for canary gating.
5) Migration converter available and documented.
